incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: TLS handshake failures > threshold for model-router -> model-backend (us-west-2). Error spike started ~1771112100. Paging oncall.
Alex (oncall): Im on it. Observed 502/524s and lots of 'tls: alert handshake failure' in router logs. Priya (net) can you join?
Priya (net): Oncall-network here. Any infra changes in the window? I see a DNS zone bulk update at 12:05 PDT (1771111800) pushing new CNAMEs for blue/green backends, and a peering rekey at 12:08 PDT.
Ben (sre): No application deploys. We did roll certs for model-backend pool at 11:58 PDT (1771111080) as part of scheduled rotation - looks successful in job output.
Alex (oncall): Sample logs from router (redacted):
```
[router] 2026-03-22T12:14:42Z error tls: alert handshake failure, conn=0x1f4 src=10.0.45.9:443 dst=10.3.11.21:5210
[router] 2026-03-22T12:14:44Z warn x509: certificate signed by unknown authority, conn=0x1f5 src=10.0.45.10:443 dst=10.3.11.22:5210
[router] 2026-03-22T12:15:00Z error tls: unexpected EOF, conn=0x1f6 src=10.0.45.11:443 dst=10.3.11.23:5210
```
Alex (oncall): Running openssl against hostname and against the resolved IP from the proxy host. `openssl s_client -connect backend.model-usw.example:5210 -servername backend.model-usw.example`:
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=2 C = US, O = Redwood, CN = Redwood Root CA
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
---
```
Alex (oncall): But when I resolve the hostname locally on the proxy (dig) I sometimes get different answers (A records point to the peering path LB vs transit-alt LB).
dns-bot: DNS audit: zone update finished at 12:05 PDT; majority of records had long TXT/CAA entries added for compliance (extra DNSSEC-looking metadata). Average UDP DNS response size increased from 480 -> 980 bytes.
Priya (net): That size could push responses into fragmentation territory (EDNS0 needed). Couple that with the peering rekey routed through an intermediate LB that has MTU 1400 on that path, we could be seeing DNS UDP truncation causing resolvers to fall back inconsistently or drop responses.
Ben (sre): I pulled a pcap from a failing proxy. Attached excerpt shows a DNS response with TC=1 (truncated) and the resolver not retrying TCP fast enough, then the proxy uses a stale cached IP that points to an older LB with an expired cert. tcpdump snippet:
```
12:14:40.123 UDP 10.0.45.9.55555 > 198.51.100.10.53: 12345+; flags: qr tc; Q:1  R:0 
12:14:40.124 proto TCP RST from 198.51.100.10: connection refused
```
Alex (oncall): So we have three moving parts: cert rotation earlier (but successful), DNS zone update increasing response sizes at 12:05, and peering rekey at 12:08. Timeline shows handshake failures start 12:12.
Priya (net): Im seeing ICMP 'fragmentation needed' messages on gw-peering-1 at 12:11-12:13. Also TCP retransmit counts spike. Looks like DNS UDP responses are getting truncated mid-path; some proxies fall back to TCP, others use old cache. Old cache can resolve to old-backend LBs with old certs or different SNI expectations. That would explain x509 unknown authority messages.
Alex (oncall): Repro steps I ran: from a proxy host: `dig +edns=0 backend.model-usw.example @198.51.100.10` returns a big UDP response with TC set. `dig +tcp @198.51.100.10 backend.model-usw.example` returns full answer pointing to 10.3.11.21. But some app instances continued using UDP cached answers.
Ben (sre): I also captured TLS handshakes. pcap shows a ClientHello from proxy to 10.3.11.21 but the ClientHello is sent, fragmented, and the ServerHello never arrives. Packets show fragments not being reassembled at the server side; 'bad record MAC' appears in some server logs when partial TLS records arrive.
Priya (net): Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Primary: DNS response size increase + intermediate MTU/peering path causing UDP truncation/inconsistent fallback -> some proxies use stale IPs -> TLS cert mismatch or connect to older LB -> handshake errors.
2) Secondary: Peering rekey caused transient packet loss and fragmentation behavior change causing TLS record fragmentation and bad_record_mac/EOF.
3) Tertiary: Cert rotation had an edge-case where some backends didn't complete chain publish -> some clients got unknown CA. Evidence currently points to networking+DNS.
Alex (oncall): Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Force proxies to use TCP for DNS for model-serving zone: `resolvconf update --zone model-serving --force-tcp` 2) Rollback DNS heavy metadata edits to shrink UDP responses (dns-bot rolled back TXT/CAA additions) 3) Route pivot: move model traffic for US-west proxies to transit-alt (higher MTU path) 4) Pause any in-flight cert rotation jobs.
dns-bot: Zone rollback applied at 12:22 PDT. DNS TCP-only enforcement rolled to 20% canary then full within 90s.
deploy-bot: route pivot deployed to 12 proxies (ids: p-41..p-52).
Alex (oncall): After forcetcp + pivot, errors on canary proxies dropped from 27% -> 1.2% within 75s. Global error rate fell to 4% (residual due to some caches in EU).
Ben (sre): Collected artifacts: pcap `1771112222_dns_frag.pcap` showing DNS TC flags + truncated UDP, `1771112222_tls_frag.pcap` showing fragmented ClientHello, tracepath outputs showing MTU 1400 on original peering path, openssl s_client outputs showing verify errors when talking to old-LB IPs. Uploaded to incident doc.
Priya (net): Actions taken: soft-restart of gw-peering-1 to clear fragmented queues and re-run PMTU probes; scheduled rolling restart of other peering gateways after reconciling MTU configs. Also added a firewall rule to not drop ICMP frag-needed.
Alex (oncall): Customer impact: ~11 enterprise tenants seeing intermittent 502/524, token throughput down ~18% at peak, median latency +90ms. CS notified.
Customer Success Bot: Interim message posted to affected accounts with ETA 45m for validation.
Nora (oncall-next): Im taking next shift at 12:40 PDT. One-line for handoff?
Alex (oncall): Handoff: P1 - TLS handshake failures starting 12:12 after DNS zone size increase + peering rekey + cert rotation earlier. Mitigated by forcing DNS-over-TCP for model-serving, rolling back DNS metadata, pivoting traffic to high-MTU transit, and pausing rotations. Residual errors in EU; monitor DNS caches and gateway restarts.
Ben (sre): Post-incident next steps (agreed): 1) Add DNS size checks to zone-update pipeline; reject edits that push UDP > 512B unless EDNS/TCP fallback validated. 2) Add EDNS/MTU probes to peering rekey playbooks. 3) Ensure cert rotations and DNS bulk updates are not simultaneous for same service (change control rule). 4) Add DNS-over-TCP as default for internal resolvers for critical services. 5) Postmortem doc + timeline + attach pcaps; CR for MTU validation on LBs.
Priya (net): Filed network change CR-3241 to enforce MTU config parity and ICMP frag-needed acceptance across peering LBs.
Nora (oncall-next): Acknowledged, will watch for regressions and coordinate on PMTU probes timeline tomorrow.
Alex (oncall): Wrapping: Ill draft the RCA with timeline / evidence / hypothesis evaluation and tag Priya/Ben. Pager off in 30m unless escalation.
